findings.reason: the fallback already has one home in `reckon/_plan_html.py`, so acting on this corrects a stale sentence about already-landed code and does not change what the node builds.
findings.text: §16 says `section_anchor`, "the one-line owner of the empty-identity fallback … that lives in routing today beside the pair and moves with it into reckon/_plan_html.py, promotion importing it from there", but §17 already moved the whole identity trio into that module (`section_record_id:71`, `section_anchor:87`, `section_id_candidates:92`), so the relocation clause describes state that no longer exists — the same module the plan elsewhere (same paragraph) says the pair already "live[s] on … since §17 landed", a self-contradiction

duplicate_owner-1.reason: the predicate applies no landing subtraction: §16 states the coverage question is the schema's, a section is outstanding until declared done whatever has landed, so it reads roadmap.implementable_sections unchanged and derives no set; promotion's pickup list subtracts landings for a different question, after a refusal; the sentence is reworded to say so

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §16 collapses a whole-document fingerprint into a section-keyed digest map (`_section_digests`) behind one module-private coverage predicate, and that predicate is the single owner of the coverage question, replacing the gate's own read (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2666`) and the sweep's (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:494`); it deletes `_AuthoredProseParser` rather than adding wrappers, so it reduces surface while hiding more behaviour behind a smaller interface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 states `section_anchor` "lives in routing today" and still needs moving, but §17 already relocated it; the owner is `reckon/_plan_html.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1480, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds exactly one public definition (`strip_tags`, → 1481) and states in its own text that it retires nothing because the identity digest and the prose walk keep their names, and that the refusal reuses the existing plan-review-missing family; §19 adds none (its expression stays private) and retires nothing.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §16 and §19 name the machinery they extend and every cited symbol exists where the plan says: `_TAG_RE`/`count_open_decisions` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1804`,`:1812`), `SECTION_NUMBER_PATTERN`/`SECTION_NUMBER_CONTINUATION` (`:64`,`:65`), `section_record_id`/`section_anchor`/`section_id_candidates` (`:71`,`:87`,`:92`), `plan_headings`/`structured_section_spans` (`:358`,`:372`), `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`/`_AuthoredProseParser`/`_authored_prose` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:148`,`:169`,`:266`), `_fingerprint_forms`/`list_plan_reviews` (`:604`,`:674`), `roadmap.implementable_sections` (`reckon/roadmap.py:107`), `recovery._plan_review_pending` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:490`), `_INVOCATION_RE` (`reckon/followup_pointers.py:43`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 states why the coverage predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review` (a join of the outstanding-section set against the union of stored section digests, over two existing readers, versus a one-record-to-one-digest match), and states why `strip_tags` exposes the module's existing tag expression rather than a parallel one, and why `count_open_decisions` keeps its bare substitution.
